images.filename: Public Lands Institute - Clifty Falls State Park - 001.tif
images.caption: Photograph by the Public Lands Institute. Site: Clifty Falls State Park, Indiana. Managed by Indiana land manager. Geological age: ~445 Mya Ordovician limestone and shale (Late Ordovician; Dillsboro Formation (shale and limestone) on lower canyon slopes; Saluda Formation (limestone and dolomite) capping waterfall crests and upper cliffs). Hydrology: Clifty Creek drains through a 300-foot-deep canyon to the Ohio River. Indigenous territories: Shawandasse Tula (Shawnee) · Myaamia (Miami); Ohio River valley ancestral Shawnee homeland; Shawnee displaced from the Ohio valley following the American Revolution; Treaty of Greenville 1795 ceded southeastern Indiana to the United States; Shawnee, Miami, and allied nations removed from Indiana under the Indian Removal Act 1830. Notable species observed: Eastern Red-backed Salamander, Marbled Salamander, Northern Dusky Salamander, dwarf larkspur, Southern Two-lined Salamander.
